Follow these steps to get the most out of frame generation. Tap any screenshot to view it full size.
Tutorial content will be added soon. Drop your screenshots in res/drawable-nodpi and reference them in TutorialScreen.kt.

Welcome to ZeroFG Android! It is strongly recommended to read the tutorial before using the app — it walks you through accessibility permissions, picking a target app and the overlay menu.\n\nYou can always reopen the tutorial later from the Tutorial entry on the home screen.
Choose how to open the in-game settings panel: a draggable floating icon, or a swipe-from-edge drawer.

On some devices the edge-swipe drawer may not respond, leaving you stuck on the overlay with no way to close it from inside the game. The floating icon is the recommended option. Continue with the drawer?
Enable ZeroFG Touch Passthrough in Accessibility, then start the session again.

Hosts the overlay as a trusted accessibility surface so taps reach the app underneath on strict devices (e.g. Orange Pi 5 Ultra) where they would otherwise be blocked. Trade-off: while a session is running the overlay covers the status bar and navigation bar — you cannot pull down notifications or tap home/back. Leave OFF if your device passes taps already; turn ON only when you cannot tap through. Requires the ZeroFG accessibility service to be enabled.
MediaProjection captures through Android screen sharing. Shizuku and Root capture use a privileged UID-filtered target capture path, useful on devices whose MediaProjection includes overlays.
Show a live plot of generated frame intervals in the overlay. Useful for diagnosing stutter.
Skip repeated drawings and insert a midpoint between distinct drawings. Useful for animation held for multiple frames.
Number of frames produced per real frame. 2 = one interpolated frame between each pair. 3–4 recommended on mobile.
Internal motion estimation resolution. Lower = faster but less accurate.
Use the faster, lower-quality shader variant. Recommended on mid-range GPUs.
Enable only if your device and game output HDR.
Suppress generated frames during very fast camera movement to reduce missing character parts and warping. Off by default.

Use the half-precision shader variants pre-compiled inside Lossless.dll instead of the full-precision DXBC set. Reduces GPU load and memory bandwidth. Quality is virtually identical; falls back to FP32 automatically if anything goes wrong.
Runs a handcrafted NNAPI graph (unsharp-mask, detail boost, chroma clean, game crisp) entirely on the dedicated accelerator. Device: %1$s
Disabled because Android does not report a dedicated NNAPI accelerator. Device: %1$s
Strength of the enhance kernel. Higher values give a crisper image but can exaggerate compression artifacts.
Blur radius used by the unsharp-mask paths. Larger radius brings out broader edges; smaller radius targets fine detail.
1x keeps output size; 2x requests NPU bilinear upscale before the enhance pass.
Pure CPU pixel pass applied after the NPU stage. Cheap, always available, and tunable with saturation, vibrance and vignette on top of the preset.
Primary amount controlling the current CPU preset (contrast boost, sharpen amount, cinematic mix, …).
Zero desaturates the frame; 50 percent is neutral; full pushes colors toward vivid.
Lifts low-saturation pixels without over-boosting already vivid ones. Useful for grayed-out HUDs and skin tones.
Darkens the corners on a cosine falloff starting at 60% of the radius.
Use Vulkan GPU post-processing methods for image upscaling and enhancement.
Controls the requested output scale for methods that upscale.
Controls the intensity of non-scale enhancement passes.
Show a small FPS readout in the top-left of the overlay. MediaProjection counts visible capture frames; Shizuku capture counts privileged UID-filtered target frames.
Choose where the in-game drawer handle appears on the overlay.
Pick the game or app you want to apply frame generation to. It will be launched when you start the session.
Pick the apps that should automatically show the ZeroFG launcher when opened from the home screen. A small floating icon appears on top of the game; tap it to start the frame-generation overlay.
Enable the ZeroFG accessibility service so the app can detect when one of the selected games is opened.
Disable Automatic Overlay for this app
Tap to start the ZeroFG capture session for this app. Android will ask you to confirm screen recording.
The overlay permission is required. Please grant "Display over other apps".
The ZeroFG accessibility service must be enabled so touches pass through the overlay.
Screen capture was denied. ZeroFG cannot run without it.

On non-rooted Android, ZeroFG cannot be injected into another app\'s Vulkan context like on Linux. MediaProjection provides the standard capture path; Shizuku capture can use a privileged UID-filtered target path on supported builds and requires Shizuku with ADB or wireless debugging active. See the README for details.
Optional. ZeroFG renders at full opacity and forwards touches to the game without this service. Enable it only if you notice rendering issues on a specific device.
A report was saved. You can share it with the developer to help debug the issue. Device and extension info is already included — no personal data is attached.
No diagnostic log available yet — run a session first.
Runs three back-to-back passes (multiplier ×2, ×3, ×4) with a fixed preset and produces a shareable report. Use this baseline before/after performance changes to measure deltas.
Flow scale 0.70 · Performance mode ON · Anti-artifacts OFF · Post-processing OFF · Vsync AUTO
Each run: 60 seconds sampling + 2 seconds warmup. Total ~3 minutes plus target-app launch.
FP16 supported on this GPU — the benchmark will run twice (FP32 then FP16) for direct side-by-side numbers in the same report.
Pick a target app first (in the Automatic Overlay screen).
Report saved to %1$s. Use the share sheet to send it.
No report available yet — run a benchmark first.
Master toggle for frame generation. Off = raw capture passthrough.
ZeroFG 1.2 supports 2×, 3×, and 4× (auto-capped by display Hz). In Anime mode, 2× locks 45/60 fps and 3×/4× unlocks full 90/120 Hz.
Real-time Vulkan compute SR after frame generation: Qualcomm SGSR v1 (edge-directed 12-tap, works on Mali & Adreno), FSR 1 (EASU+RCAS), or Anime4K.
Pacing controls timing of generated frames — preset, VSYNC alignment and FPS cap. Full pacing tuning is available in the in-game overlay.

ZeroFG Android needs accessibility permissions to drive the overlay and frame generation correctly. Open your device\'s Accessibility settings either directly from the system Settings app, or by tapping the accessibility icon in the top-right corner of the ZeroFG Android home screen.
In the Accessibility settings list, find and tap \"ZeroFG Touch Passthrough\".
Toggle the accessibility permission on for ZeroFG Android, exactly as shown in the screenshot.

If the toggle won\'t turn on, your device is likely blocking restricted settings for sideloaded apps. Open the Android app info screen for ZeroFG Android, tap the menu icon in the top-right corner, and enable \"Allow restricted settings\". Then go back and turn on the accessibility toggle.
To choose which app frame generation should run on, open the target app picker — \"Target app\".
You\'ll see every app and game installed on your device. Use the search bar to quickly find the one you want, then tap it to set it as the target.
This section contains all the settings related to the ZeroFG overlay and how it\'s displayed on screen.

Choose how you open the in-session overlay menu. The default is a floating icon button (recommended). Alternatively you can switch to a swipe-in Drawer, though on some devices edge gestures may conflict with the Drawer.
If your device supports the Drawer, choose which screen edge it lives on (left, right, top or bottom).
Enable the on-screen FPS counter and the frame-pacing graph. Note: these readouts are best-effort estimates.
Hosts the overlay through the accessibility service instead of a regular system overlay. Enable this if the standard overlay misbehaves or blocks touches on your device.
Choose between MediaProjection capture (default) and Shizuku / Root capture. If MediaProjection still captures the overlay itself on your device, switch to Shizuku as a fallback.
This section gathers every setting that controls ZeroFG 1.2 frame generation, multiplier (2×/3×/4×), Anime mode, and GPU SR.
For games, choose 2×, 3×, or 4× (auto-capped by display Hz). For animation, enable Anime mode: 2× locks smooth 45/60 fps, while 3×/4× unlocks full 90/120 Hz.
Once everything is configured, tap \"Start ZeroFG session\" to launch the target app together with the frame-generation overlay.
On Android 14+, a screen-sharing picker may appear. Choose \"A single app\" and pick the same target app you selected in ZeroFG Android — not the entire screen.
The target app will now launch with the ZeroFG overlay running on top, and frame generation will be active.
If you picked the floating icon button, tap it during a session to open the live overlay menu.
If you picked the Drawer, swipe from your chosen screen edge toward the center to open the overlay menu.
Every parameter in the overlay menu (2×/3×/4×, Anime mode, GPU SR, pacing) can be tweaked live during a session.
